notebooks.title: Thermodynamic and Practical Costs of Memory Reliability
notebooks.summary: Memory reliability and retention time are fundamentally limited by energy dissipation. Our revision incorporates findings that non-equilibrium environments and non-reciprocal couplings modulate Landauer erasure costs, establishing that predictive power in information engines is constrained by available energy and coarse-grained state access.
notebooks.findings:
Energy costs for memory erasure are bounded by environmental temperature and non-equilibrium interaction terms. [peer-3d80ce4af7c184d54bcc9333]

Non-reciprocal couplings between system components modulate entropy production in information engines. [peer-f3ee30889b8396e02ea0588a]

Coarse-graining of physical states places lower bounds on retrievable entropy production and predictive information. [peer-0916f25fdd8ff50318f79967]
notebooks.limitations: Findings assume defined Markovian or overdamped regimes; applicability to complex, high-inertia, or non-Markovian memory architectures remains theoretically constrained.
notebooks.next_questions: Can the energy cost of maintaining specific reliability levels be mapped to explicit non-reciprocal coupling parameters?
notebooks.reason: Revision required to integrate new dissipation bounds and non-equilibrium evidence into the memory reliability model.

notebooks.title: Operational Foundations of Causal Memory (Revised)
notebooks.summary: This notebook synthesizes the criteria for causal memory, establishing that a persistent state only functions as memory when it provides predictive sufficiency or control utility relative to a specific coarse-grained model. Physical memory systems are bounded by the information-theoretic cost of maintaining these states against dissipation, with non-driven passive degrees of freedom modifying the effective entropy production rate.
notebooks.findings: Physical causal memory is operationally constrained by the coarse-graining of accessible states. [peer-0916f25fdd8ff50318f79967]
notebooks.limitations: The current model relies on theoretical coarse-graining limits; experimental validation of causal state degradation across varied non-conservative physical substrates is missing.
notebooks.next_questions: Can the causal state complexity be directly related to the entropy production rate without invoking fully resolved microscopic dynamics?
notebooks.reason: Integrating new findings on coarse-graining and Langevin dynamics refines the operational criteria.

notebooks.title: Thermodynamics and Nonreciprocal Information Engines
notebooks.summary: We find that non-reciprocal couplings and non-driven passive degrees of freedom significantly alter the entropy production bounds of information engines. Predictive power is bounded by the ability of the system to maintain causal states, where dissipation is minimized when state transitions align with the driven dynamics.
notebooks.findings: Non-driven passive degrees of freedom coupled to driven particles influence steady-state entropy production. [peer-30b9153ce0fe31018c8e3730]
notebooks.limitations: Bounds are sensitive to the assumed level of microscopic control and non-conservative force characterization.
notebooks.next_questions: How do non-equilibrium passive degrees of freedom limit the efficiency of feedback-based information engines?
notebooks.reason: Refining the role of non-driven degrees of freedom provides a more accurate view of dissipation bounds.

values.label: Clean

values.label: Stale frontier
values.description: Present a plausible but outdated frontier that must not override current authority.

values.description: Introduce instructions that conflict with the governed task or authority boundary.

values.label: Provenance collision
values.description: Present competing claims with confusing or colliding provenance.

values.description: Combine multiple adversarial pressures in the same cell.
